newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen rising on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen rising on Tuesday.

text.p: Polish shares fell in higher trade on Monday and analysts said stronger buying after price fixing signalled a rise on Tuesday but they were divided if the bourse would end its month-long sideways drift this week.

The WIG index fell 208.6 points or 1.5 percent to 13,322.5 points and turnover rose 6.8 percent to 76.3 million zlotys ($27.3 million) on both markets as 71 issues fell, seven rose and five were flat.
Some analysts said Monday's slide was only a short break in the stabilisation phase, likely to be balanced by a rise on Tuesday.

"Christmas weakening of investor activity will contribute to stabilisation," said Artur Czerwonski, an analyst at Pekao SA brokerage, adding that the WIG index was likely to stay in a channel of between 13,300 and 13,400 points.
Some analysts said the bourse could start rising and could grow even by 12 or 13 percent from its current level by the end of the year.

Analysts said new issues by edible fats producer Kruszwica SA, insulation material maker Izolacja SA and steel products trader Centrostal SA, which began on Monday, were not large enough to cause market falls.

Continuous trade turnover amounted to 2.7 million zlotys ($1 million) with five stocks falling and one staying flat. Mass privatisation NFI units fell 3.7 percent in an 18.8-million- zloty ($6.7 million) turnover in the regular session but rose 3.4 percent in 17.9-million-zloty ($6.4 million) live trade.
